title: It didn't. One man's mistake at a press conference did.
description:
It didn't. One man's mistake at a press conference did. On 9 November 1989, a Politburo spokesman was handed a note on new travel rules minutes before facing reporters, with no time to be briefed on it properly.

East German Politburo spokesman. Read from a note he barely understood, live, in front of the world's press.

"When does this take effect?" Schabowski shuffled his papers, looked uncertain, then said: 'As far as I know, immediately, without delay.' The rules weren't due to start until 4am the next morning.

By nightfall, thousands stood at the checkpoints demanding to cross. Border guards had no orders for this. No shots, no directive from above, just a crowd too large to hold back.

At 11:30pm, a single guard at Bornholmer Straße opened the gate. Nobody above him had decided to.
